terms.grammar: quōminus with the subjunctive after a verb of hindering
evidence: Traupman 101: quid tenuit quō minus venīrēs?
terms.comment: The construction (tenēre quōminus) is classical; the question as such is Traupman’s. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

evidence: Erasm. Coll., Fōrm., In culpā, in causā, in morā, I 68

phrases.latin: Tū nōbīs in morā fuistī. Tū semper in morā es. Quid tē remorātum est?
phrases.english: You held us up; you’re always the one we wait for; what kept you?
phrases.source: Erasm. Coll., Fōrm., In culpā, in causā, in morā, I 68

sources: Lewis & Short: teneo · Lewis & Short: quominus · Lewis & Short: remoror
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 101, 328, 336.
Erasmus from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-erasmus), a non-classical school text, checked against the edition named there.
